title: Sort a Stack
description:
`stack` is given bottom-first, so the last element is the top. Sort it so the largest value ends on top, using only stack operations and recursion — no arrays or library sorts.

Return the sorted stack in the same bottom-first form.

**Constraints**

- `0 <= stack length <= 2000`
- `-10^9 <= value <= 10^9`
hints: Pop everything, then insert each value back into the already sorted remainder.

editorial.explanation:
Sorting with only stack operations is insertion sort in disguise.

Pop a value from the source, then push back everything on the sorted stack that is larger than it
before placing it — that keeps the sorted stack ordered at all times.

`O(n^2)` time, `O(n)` space. The recursive version replaces the second stack with the call stack.
